issue: After an automatic upgrade, all network rules were removed and caused a 24h duration outage of all their Cilium protected Kubernetes clusters in all their regions and cloud providers.
root_cause: The root cause was an automatic security update to systemd on March 8, 2023, at 06:00 UTC. This update triggered a latent interaction in the network stack, causing systemd-networkd to forcibly delete routing rules managed by the Cilium Container Network Interface (CNI) plugin.
solution: All services were operational by March 9, 08:58 UTC, and the incident was fully resolved, including historical data backfill, by March 10, 06:25 UTC. This update triggered a latent interaction in the network stack, causing systemd-networkd to forcibly delete routing rules managed by the Cilium Container Network Interface (CNI) plugin.

issue: A staged Kubernetes upgrade of CircleCI's main production cluster left `kube-proxy` and `kubelet` at incompatible versions.
root_cause: The change between versions altered the format of `kube-proxy`'s `iptables` rulesets, so as pods churned and `Endpoints` objects changed, `kube-proxy`'s `Proxier.syncProxyRules ` (an `iptables-save` / `iptables-restore` read-modify-write) repeatedly hit "Sync failed" errors, leaving the per-node iptables in a corrupted state and silently breaking service-to-service routing across the cluster.
solution: Recovery required a full node-by-node cluster restart and triggered two follow-on incidents.

issue: Login page and dashboard briefly show odd cross-account data before the site goes fully down for maintenance.
root_cause: Queues used to hold requests and responses for an AI system's cache became corrupted and got out of sequence, which meant some responses were served to the wrong user, unintentionally revealing details like another user's activity history and some billing information.
solution: Took the affected system down while the sequencing bug in the cache/queue handling was fixed, and notified affected users about what categories of information may have been exposed to someone else.

issue: ChatGPT offline; users exposed to other active users' chat titles and payment details.
root_cause: A bug in the redis-py Redis client library caused connections to be recycled with incorrect session context under heavy load.
solution: Patched the redis-py library to clear connection state upon context validation failure.

issue: OpenAI Moderation endpoint requests experiencing high latency and HTTP 504 timeouts.
root_cause: A database scale-up in the moderation policy registry caused write deadlocks on the moderation servers.
solution: Aborted the policy scale-up and optimized database lock parameters in the moderation service.

issue: Google Cloud VMware Engine (GCVE) customer clusters were automatically deleted, causing permanent data loss.
root_cause: Initial GCVE provisioning was done using a legacy option with a fixed-term contract that lacked automatic renewal, triggering automated deletion workflows at the end of the term.
solution: Restored customer workloads from external backups and updated internal provisioning accounts to prevent automatic expiration of infrastructure services.

issue: New authorizations and deployments failing platform-wide with a database-level error, unrelated to any application code change.
root_cause: A foreign key column was defined with a smaller integer data type than the primary key column it referenced. When the primary key's values exceeded what the smaller foreign-key type could hold, inserts began failing with an overflow error, blocking creation of new authorizations, downstream, new deployments.
solution: Corrected the mismatched column data type so the foreign key could represent the full range of primary key values, resolving the overflow and restoring the ability to create authorizations and deployments.

issue: Heroku Connect sync between Salesforce and Postgres failing.
root_cause: An API update in Salesforce modified field serialization order, breaking the parsing logic in Heroku Connect.
solution: Released a client parser hotfix that supports dynamic field indexing, and restarted sync workers.

issue: Elevated error rates and timeout latencies for AWS Lambda invocations in US-East-1.
root_cause: A configuration deployment to Lambda routing proxies caused CPU starvation under peak load.
solution: Rolled back the proxy configuration changes and scaled routing nodes to handle load.

issue: SMS and push notifications delayed for several minutes.
root_cause: A downstream SMS aggregator network connection degraded, backing up notification dispatcher buffers.
solution: Switched traffic to backup SMS providers and increased dispatcher queue capacities.

issue: API calls unexpectedly getting rate-limited far more often than usual after a routine maintenance window.
root_cause: Maintenance on the API token-management system inadvertently changed how token validation interacted with the rate-limiting system, causing much stricter rate-limit enforcement to be applied broadly, including to calls that should have been exempt.
solution: Reverted the token-validation/rate-limiting interaction to the correct behavior; added monitoring so this kind of enforcement-rate spike is caught automatically instead of relying on customer reports.

issue: OpenAI Fine-Tuning API jobs failing to start or stuck in execution.
root_cause: A thread pool exhaustion in the fine-tuning orchestrator blocked job schedule queues.
solution: Increased fine-tuning orchestrator thread pool sizes and scaled computing nodes.

issue: All crate downloads from crates.io failed for 13 minutes, causing millions of failed cargo build requests.
root_cause: A deployment introduced a bug in the download URL generation logic, causing it to return malformed URLs for all download requests.
solution: Rolled back the deployment and added unit tests covering download URL generation.

issue: On July 25th, 2023, we experienced a total Honeycomb outage.
root_cause: It impacted all user-facing components from 1:40 p.m. UTC to 2:48 p.m. UTC, during which no data could be processed or accessed.
solution: The full details of incident triage process is covered in here.

issue: ChatGPT Plugin Directory unavailable or returning connection errors.
root_cause: A bug in the plugin directory search service triggered query parsing infinite loops under specific text symbols.
solution: Patched the directory search query parser code and restarted search API nodes.

issue: 1.1.1.1 public DNS resolver returning SERVFAIL responses.
root_cause: DNSSEC validation failed in resolver software after a key rotation mismatch caused invalid signatures.
solution: Temporarily disabled DNSSEC checks, synced keys, and re-enabled validation.

issue: ChatGPT API and web interface experiencing high error rates and timeouts.
root_cause: A distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack saturated the edge proxies and gateway controllers.
solution: Implemented stricter WAF rate-limiting rules and isolated traffic from known malicious IP blocks.

issue: Multiple SimpleDB storage nodes lost power simultaneously in one US-East data center.
root_cause: The lock service de-registered them rapidly, which spiked load and pushed handshake latencies above SimpleDB's too-aggressive handshake timeout. Healthy storage and metadata nodes failed their handshakes, removed themselves from the cluster, and couldn't rejoin because the metadata nodes that would authorize them had also taken themselves out.
solution: Recovery required manually raising the handshake timeout and restarting metadata nodes.

issue: A "network disruption" caused metadata services to experience load that caused response times to exceed timeout values, causing storage nodes to take themselves down.
root_cause: This disruption caused storage servers to query the internal metadata service for their membership assignments. The root cause was a combination of factors.
solution: Nodes that took themselves down continued to retry, ensuring that load on metadata services couldn't decrease.

issue: ChatGPT users exposed to other active chat session data.
root_cause: A race condition in session mapping logic during high traffic volume peaks mixed up user context keys.
solution: Implemented strict session-isolation scopes and refactored thread locks on connection managers.

issue: GitHub Actions workflow queues delayed and runner communication failing.
root_cause: Redis connection limits on the orchestrator were exceeded due to a connection leak introduced in a worker service deployment.
solution: Rolled back the worker deployment, terminated leaky connections, and raised limits.

issue: GitHub write operations degraded, and repository updates delayed for several hours.
root_cause: A network partition between data centers triggered automated primary promotion, but the chosen replica had stale replication streams.
solution: Manually forced failover to the correct database node and restarted write operations.

issue: A Kinesis cell newly migrated to a new architecture had an unusually high number of very low-throughput shards.
root_cause: The cell management system distributed the shards unevenly, so a few hosts ended up handling huge numbers of shards and produced abnormally large status messages. The system misinterpreted slow status messages as host failures, kicked off a redistribution storm, and overloaded the secure-connection provisioning subsystem.
solution: CloudWatch Logs, S3 event notifications, Firehose, ECS, Lambda, Redshift, MWAA, and Glue all degraded for ~7 hours.

issue: Site-wide read outage after a routine database configuration rollout.
root_cause: A configuration change rolled out to production databases changed how hosts responded to routing-service health checks. The health-check system incorrectly marked the read-only endpoint as unhealthy, taking it out of rotation even though the databases themselves were fine.
solution: Reverted the configuration change to restore correct health-check responses; read traffic resumed within the hour once the endpoint was marked healthy again.

issue: Git clones and pushes failing intermittently due to file server errors.
root_cause: A file storage array array controller hardware failure led to data corruption on primary volumes.
solution: Activated secondary controller paths and synchronized volumes from replica logs.

issue: GitHub Gists and Pages unavailable, returning database errors.
root_cause: An unoptimized search query triggered database write locks, exhausting active connection pools.
solution: Optimized the query, terminated locking transactions, and added database rate limits.

issue: Webhook delivery delays of up to several hours.
root_cause: A queue queue capacity limit bug in the webhook broker caused delivery worker starvation.
solution: Pushed a hotfix to expand queue capacities and scaled consumer nodes.

issue: Long outage of a data-center-hosted service; on-site staff unable to resolve it quickly on their own.
root_cause: A control-plane and analytics system running across three physically separate data centers relied on a colocation provider's backup power arrangement. When utility power was interrupted, the backup generator arrangement didn't behave as expected, and it took considerable time to get clarity from the colocation provider on why, since key technical details about their power failover setup weren't fully documented or communicated in advance.
solution: Worked with the colocation provider to restore power and bring systems back online, then pushed to get full documentation of the provider's power failover design and clearer communication commitments for any future incident of this kind.

issue: New feature under heavy testing causes hangs and crashes in the test suite, but only intermittently and only with the new code path.
root_cause: A months-long performance rewrite of core I/O handling introduced a native code path (needed because the new high-performance async I/O API wasn't available in managed code). The new code had a subtle interlocking bug that only manifested as a race condition under certain timing conditions, making it hang or crash unpredictably rather than failing consistently.
solution: Caught during testing rather than in production; resolved by isolating and fixing the specific interlock logic in the native code path, after extended debugging effort by multiple engineers.

issue: Dashboard, mobile app, and API all briefly unavailable at the same time shortly after a database version upgrade.
root_cause: After a Postgres major-version upgrade, an audit-logging extension that had passed staging tests was re-enabled in production. A routine table-creation migration triggered a pathological interaction with that extension, which hung while holding critical locks and ignored timeout signals, blocking other database operations across multiple products at once.
solution: Restarted the primary database to forcibly break the deadlock (a short hard outage), then removed the problematic extension entirely rather than attempting to reconfigure it.

issue: GitHub API returning HTTP 503 errors and blocking Git operations.
root_cause: A faulty routing policy deployed to the API gateway caused request routing redirect loops.
solution: Reverted the API gateway routing configuration and restarted edge proxies.

issue: Gist read/write operations experiencing intermittent failures.
root_cause: Redis session cluster for Gists became saturated due to a connection leak in Gist client components.
solution: Patched the Gist client wrapper to correctly release connections and restarted the session cluster.

issue: Repository archiving and download requests failing with HTTP 504 gateway timeouts.
root_cause: Storage mount disk latency spiked in the archive storage array because of a disk controller card failure.
solution: Replaced the failed storage array controller card and synchronized data streams.

issue: Legitimate customer traffic being blocked by the web application firewall with no recent deploys to explain it.
root_cause: A gap in access controls allowed a change to be made to a firewall configuration outside of the normal infrastructure-as-code pipeline. Because the change wasn't recorded in the deployment history, on-call responders spent significant time chasing unrelated leads (like recent code deploys and CORS errors) before automated drift detection revealed the untracked firewall change as the real cause.
solution: Reverted the out-of-band firewall change and tightened access controls so that infrastructure changes outside the standard pipeline are blocked or immediately flagged.

issue: CircleCI build workflow triggering and job scheduling suffered major delays following a database upgrade.
root_cause: A major-version blue/green database upgrade succeeded, but a secondary update immediately after rendered the database query optimizer statistics stale. Without indexes, all queries ran full table scans against disk.
solution: Re-promoted the blue (old) database to quickly restore operations, and adjusted the migration sequence to run ANALYZE immediately post-cutover.

issue: GitHub API Gateway returning high TLS handshake timeouts for developer queries.
root_cause: A configuration drift in API gateway SSL cipher settings caused CPU exhaustion on load balancers during peak traffic.
solution: Reverted the SSL cipher configuration changes to the standard set.

issue: Issues, Projects, and Milestones creation failing with internal database write locks.
root_cause: A routine database index optimization job on the main tickets table acquired exclusive tables locks under active load.
solution: Terminated the optimization job, optimized locking queries, and deferred indexes build.

issue: A policy change containing blank fields triggered a null pointer exception in Service Control, Google's API management and control plane system.
root_cause: The code path that failed was not feature flag protected and lacked proper error handling. When the policy data replicated globally, it caused Service Control binaries to crash loop across all regions. While a red-button fix was deployed within 40 minutes, larger regions like us-central-1 experienced extended recovery times (up to 2h 40m) due to a thundering herd problem when Service Control tasks restarted, overloading the underlying Spanner infrastructure.
solution: The incident affected Google and Google Cloud APIs globally, with recovery times varying by product architecture.

issue: GitHub Actions orchestrator experiencing slow run initiations.
root_cause: A memory leak in the runner orchestration Go service led to slow garbage collection sweeps, increasing scheduling times.
solution: Rolled back the orchestrator service release to a stable version and debugged the leak.

issue: Webhook notifications and integrations processing delayed by up to 30 minutes.
root_cause: A database schema change in the integration metadata table locked query execution paths in the delivery worker broker.
solution: Rolled back the schema change and rescheduled the update for off-peak hours.

issue: GitHub Pages deployment pipelines stuck in queued state.
root_cause: A certificate renewal task hung in a locked state, blocking subsequent deployment queue consumers.
solution: Killed the blocked renewal task, restarted deployment worker services, and added execution timeouts.

issue: Pull Requests pages loading slowly or failing to render diffs.
root_cause: A high volume of concurrent commits to monorepos triggered lock queues on git file servers.
solution: Adjusted PR diff-rendering concurrency limits and enabled aggressive diff caching rules.

issue: SSH and HTTPS Git authentication failing intermittently for over an hour.
root_cause: A memory allocation failure in the internal user-session cache cluster led to authentication lookups falling back to slow DB paths.
solution: Restarted the affected cache nodes and increased cache cluster RAM allocation limits.

issue: The website for Xubuntu, a derivative of Ubuntu Linux that uses Xfce as its desktop environment, was compromised by an attacker who changed download links to a malicious zip file.
root_cause: The incident was caused by a malicious actor who gained unauthorized access to the WordPress installation maintaining the Xubuntu website.
solution: As a long-term remediation, the Xubuntu team decided to migrate their website to Hugo, a static site generator, to eliminate the type of attack vector exploited.

issue: Widespread cloud service disruption, new connections to a core database service failing region-wide.
root_cause: A latent race condition in the automated DNS-management system for a managed database service caused two internal automation components to overwrite each other's DNS update, ultimately leaving an empty DNS record for the service's regional endpoint. Because so many other services depended on this database for internal coordination, the DNS failure cascaded into compute provisioning and other control-plane systems.
solution: Engineers manually restored the correct DNS records and disabled the automation that caused the conflict while it was fixed. Downstream systems that had accumulated bad state (like stale leases) needed additional manual recovery time even after the DNS issue itself was resolved.

issue: The AWS us-east-1 outage degraded EC2/Lambda/DynamoDB/Route 53, leaving Launchdarkly's US web app, API, and client-side streaming SDKs unable to autoscale and dropping events.
root_cause: The initial phase was triggered by a major AWS us-east-1 outage, which degraded services like EC2, Lambda, DynamoDB, and Route 53. This caused excessive retries from SDKs, overwhelming the streaming service and its load balancer, which then became unresponsive.
solution: After AWS recovered, an internal change meant to shed load reverted flag-delivery to a legacy routing path with cold caches; SDKs hammered the streaming service with retries, the load balancer became unresponsive, and EC2 provisioning issues prevented scale-out, taking server-side streaming globally to ~99% errors and keeping US streaming down for another ~12 hours.

issue: The AWS us-east-1 outage, incident.io's Google-Cloud-hosted platform mostly held but third-party AWS dependencies cascaded into a complex multi-team response: their telecom provider's outage backed up the on-call notification queue (~30× normal load), their deploy pipeline was wedged because their builder transitively pulled `golang:1.24.9-alpine` from Docker Hub (which runs on AWS), and Postgres dead tuples in the escalation-acquisition index turned scaling up workers into a net throughput regression.
root_cause: Although incident.io's core platform is hosted on Google Cloud, several key services were impacted due to dependencies on AWS-hosted third parties. Specific failures included Scribe being unable to join calls from 07:34 to 10:07 UTC and again from 12:40 to 17:37 UTC due to an AWS-hosted transcription provider.
solution: A traffic-management feature flag also failed to apply globally because of a recent "top 10 orgs by volume" usability tweak.

issue: GitHub Copilot completions experiencing timeouts and failed requests.
root_cause: A configuration drift in the model gateway proxies restricted keep-alive socket reuse, flooding backend clusters.
solution: Corrected the proxy configuration setting and re-aligned keep-alive parameters across regions.

issue: Global CDN and proxy outage after an internal permissions change.
root_cause: A permissions update on an internal analytics database changed how a query returned table metadata, causing it to unexpectedly return duplicate rows. This bloated a configuration file used by the bot-detection system beyond a hard-coded size limit, which crashed the proxy software that handles most customer traffic.
solution: Rolled back to a last-known-good version of the configuration file to restore traffic, then fixed the query and added stricter validation and size limits on generated configuration files before they are distributed network-wide.

issue: Codespaces creation and session loading experiencing elevated latency.
root_cause: Hypervisor host connection limit reached in the primary region due to slow container cleanup routines.
solution: Manually purged idle hypervisor containers and optimized cleanup daemon check frequencies.

issue: All virtual machine provisioning operations (Actions, Codespaces) failed globally for over five hours.
root_cause: A telemetry configuration gap caused security policies to be automatically applied to backend storage accounts, which blocked critical VM metadata access in the underlying cloud provider.
solution: Reverted the auto-applied security policies and added telemetry validation checks to prevent incorrect policy enforcement.

issue: GitHub Package Registry publishing operations delayed or returning HTTP 500 errors.
root_cause: An unindexed metadata lookup query in the registry backend database triggered 100% CPU lock on active read replicas.
solution: Pushed an indexing migration script to the database and scaled up registry replica pools.

issue: API error rates climb steadily over several hours with no single obvious trigger, unlike a typical sudden outage.
root_cause: Frontend traffic increased gradually while a backend database service was already running close to capacity; a database index design concentrated certain metadata on only a few shards, and a short cache expiration time forced frequent database refreshes, so read contention on those few shards grew disproportionately as traffic rose.
solution: According to the incident report, mitigations focused on redistributing the concentrated metadata across more shards and lengthening the cache expiration window to reduce refresh frequency and read contention.
note: This detail appeared inside a third-party aggregator page alongside an unrelated Slack incident; verify against Google's own incident report before relying on it for evaluation.

issue: 13 min read Summary of Windows Azure Service Disruption on Feb 29th, 2012 By The Microsoft Azure Team, view all posts by this author Share Link copied to clipboard!
root_cause: Certificates that were valid for one year were created. Instead of using an appropriate library, someone wrote code that computed one year to be the current date plus one year. On February 29th 2012, this resulted in the creation of certificates with an expiration date of February 29th 2013, which were rejected because of the invalid date. This caused an Azure global outage that lasted for most of a day.
solution: That point the FC stops all internally initiated software updates and automatic service healing is disabled. To prevent customers from inadvertently causing further impact to their running applications, unsuccessfully scaling-out their applications, and fruitlessly trying to deploy new applications, we disabled service management functionality in all clusters worldwide.

issue: Receiving full sync requests from each redis-slave caused the master to suffer extreme load, resulting in performance degradation of the master and timeouts from redis-slaves to redis-master.
root_cause: In 2013, a temporary network partition in the redis cluster used for billing operations, caused a massive resynchronization from slaves. The overloaded master crashed and when it was restarted, it started up in read-only mode. The auto-recharge component in This resulted in failed transactions from Twilio's auto-recharge service, which unfortunately billed the customers before updating their balance internally. So the auto-recharge system continued to retry the transaction again and again, resulting in multiple charges to customer's credit cards.
solution: Some accounts were suspended as a result of a recharge attempted against a credit card deactivated by the repeated billing. /: Our on-call engineers restarted the redis-master to address the high load.

issue: 2013–09–17 Outage Postmortem Xandr Engineering Follow 6 min read · -- 1 Listen Share On starting at ( America/New_York) the AppNexus platform experienced a technical failure that initially fully halted ad serving and later partially degraded ad serving with the entire incident lasting approximately two and a half hours.
root_cause: A double free revealed by a database update caused all "impression bus" servers to crash simultaneously. This wasn't caught in staging and made it into production because a time delay is required to trigger the bug, and the staging period didn't have a built-in delay.
solution: By ( America/New_York), one engineering team restored enough capacity in our Amsterdam data center (AMS1) to service 50% of Amsterdam’s regular volume of direct transactions. Our engineers restored service in AMS1 using a new snapshot of data from the internal database.

issue: Outage post. Outage post-mortem - Dropbox Outage post-mortem // By Akhil Gupta.
root_cause: In this case, a bug in the script caused the upgrade to run on a handful of machines serving production traffic.
solution: The service was back up and running about three hours later, with core service fully restored by PT on Sunday.

issue: Npm Blog Archive: Four hours of partial outage, 2014. npm Blog Archive: Four hours of partial outage, 2014-02-24 The npm blog has been discontinued.
root_cause: The root cause is that a bug in HAProxy causes it to leak file descriptors, resulting in slow or non-responsive connections.
solution: Joyent has confirmed that they restarted the system that was leaking file descriptors, and they’re in the process of building a more permanent fix.

issue: Npm Blog Archive: Seven minutes of registry partial outage, 2014. npm Blog Archive: Seven minutes of registry partial outage, 2014-02-21 The npm blog has been discontinued.
root_cause: Seven minutes of registry partial outage, 2014-02-21 For 7 minutes this morning, from about 5.43 to Pacific Time, the registry was mostly unavailable due to another data center network issue.

issue: Npm Blog Archive: Registry downtime 2014. npm Blog Archive: Registry downtime 2014-02-16 The npm blog has been discontinued.
root_cause: The root cause was network issues with our hosting provider, Joyent, possibly related to a DDoS attack on another provider at that same facility.

issue: Service disruption at Knight Capital (see incident report).
root_cause: A combination of conflicting deployed versions and re-using a previously used bit caused a $460M loss. See also a longer write-up.
solution: Knight did not have a second technician review this deployment and no one at Knight realized that the Power Peg code had not been removed from the eighth server, nor the new RLP code added. The email messages references SMARS and identified an error as “Power Peg disabled.” there were 97 of these emails sent to Knight personnel.

issue: Partial outage in Buffalo, New York. The outage happened due to large scale 140 Gigabit DDoS Attack.
root_cause: The network engineers are currently working on identifying the root cause of this outage.
solution: However, the attack was mitigated and network connectivity was restored in full within 7 minutes.

issue: Grab You Some Post. Given the importance of such reports, it was surprising to find numerous incidents recorded as shown: 2015-02-0211pm XXX Service Went Down At hrs, we experienced downtime in XXX service.
root_cause: We looked through the logs and found a bug in DB connections leading to memory leaks.
solution: Any practice that is currently leading to potential miscommunications should be removed or improved upon. Solution The issue was temporarily resolved by a rollback to version 1.2.3.

issue: 19 Minute Check-in Blackout. Snitch check-ins were accepted but not processed.
root_cause: We have discovered that check-ins were not run due to incorrectly telling our queue that we had failed a message.

issue: Incorrect DOWN reports. During the outage we failed to alert on missed snitch check-ins and sent a large number of erroneous failure alerts for healthy snitches.
root_cause: On March 6th at we deployed a change that decoupled two of the models in our system (historical periods and check-ins).
solution: We were alerted immediately disabled our alerter process to avoid further confusion. We began diagnosing the cause and at deployed a fix for the unscoped delete.

issue: Emergency Update to VPS Hypervisors. Our clients using the Budget VPS Services may have noticed a brief service disruption.
root_cause: This disruption was due to a emergency maintenance which took place to update critical OS Libraries.

issue: Degraded event processing.
root_cause: We are anticipating more blips due to the saturated network equipment until we can cut over to the upgraded equipment, and will record those here.
solution: The fix has proven insufficient for our load as of and our service provider is working on installing upgraded network equipment. Our provider has corrected the issue and data processing has caught up and is now occurring normally.

issue: Issue in API Production Environment.
root_cause: This issue was caused by a leap second adjustment in the operating system adversely affecting a configuration service on one of the backend servers.
solution: We have upgraded the operating system, which will prevent this issue from happening in future.

issue: Website Not Loading with Busy Message. Current investigating reports of website not loading.
root_cause: Could not find issues with server being overloaded, checked with hosting provider for possible regional outage.
solution: Restarted servers to be safe, had users reporting issue confirm on multiple devices.

issue: Emergency Reboot for KVM Hypervisors.
root_cause: Due to a bug that affects libvir when updating CentOS 6.6 to CentOS 6.7, we had to conduct an emergency reboot for the Hypervisors.

issue: Issue in API Production Environment (US). During this time, a small number of events (~50) failed to process, resulting in outdated analytics for a handful of learners.
root_cause: This was caused by a misconfiguration in our event store system, which has now been rectified.

issue: DNS outage. Our domain registrar has caused a major outage to our domain this morning.
root_cause: Due to the way that domain names and DNS work, you may have issues accessing your mumble server and/or our website until the DNS cache clears.

issue: ACP Tools App: iOS9 "Invalid Credentials" Error Blocks Logins.
root_cause: The update that fixes this issue is available for download on the App Store. Attempting to sign in with any credentials (valid or otherwise) will always show the error message "Invalid Credentials." This does not mean your password is invalid and you do not need to reset it.

issue: Network issues in Multiple Datacenters. We are in constant contact, however its slow moving as the attacker keeps changing his attack vectors.
root_cause: Our upstream provider reports that they've made some progress on mitigating the numerous DoS on their infrastructure, but due to the varying nature of the target, scope, and size of the attacks, network connectivity has not yet been restored.
solution: We are monitoring to confirm this." There was a small localized outage a few moments ago (which has been resolved), but the brunt of the attack was properly mitigated.

issue: A Key Expired in Redis, You Won't Believe What Happened Next.
root_cause: In this particular case, we found that apart from the usual minuscule DB replication lag, a region-specific change in Unicorns took up to 60 minutes to reach our consumers.
solution: Footnotes ElastiCache is hardly elastic, considering your “scale up” is a deliberate process involving backup, replicate, deploy, and switch, during which time your server is serving peak hour teapots (as reads and writes may be disabled).

issue: Issue in API Production Environment (US).
root_cause: This was caused by one of Knewton platform services temporarily going down due to a deployment misconfiguration.
solution: We restarted the service and operations returned to normal.

issue: Problems with swedish numbers.
root_cause: We identified a problem with the concatenation of messages, and are working to fix it. An issue with long messages was identified, messages are being rerouted and monitored.

issue: On-going DoS attack. In total, we suffered from 10 minutes of downtime, and a further 20 minutes of increased platform response time (meaning that accessing your files via a web browser was dreadfully slow).
root_cause: Eventually the Web App became inaccessible due to our Apache web servers being saturated with TCP connections.
solution: The Web App was then restored to a normal state.

issue: Network Outage. We are experiencing a network outage in our Dallas Cloud Location and we are presently investigating the issue.
root_cause: The root cause was an unannounced upstream network upgrade which resulted in an unforeseen outage affecting a number of BGP Sessions, including DigitalFyre's.

issue: Issue With Emailing Scheduled Legacy Reports.
root_cause: The bug itself has been fixed and all Report Wizard reports have been generated properly.

issue: V1 downtime. We are currently investigating unusual traffic on Siteleaf v1 which resulted in intermittent downtime late Saturday night.
root_cause: We determined the issue was caused by a bad IP assigned to one of our load balancers by AWS, our hosting provider.

issue: Enterprise API production environment Europe.
root_cause: This incident was caused by a connection failure between two of our backend services. Our technical team has put processes in place to mitigate connection failures of this type moving forward.

issue: Npm Blog Archive: package tarball read outage today. npm Blog Archive: package tarball read outage today The npm blog has been discontinued.
root_cause: 8am: The root cause of the issue was identified as a negative file modification times for the specific affected tarballs. A new script was immediately run to fix mtimes on all tarball files appearing in the logs as producing 502 errors.
solution: We cleared up the known issue in the mistaken belief that this was causing the 502s.

issue: Issue in API Production Environment (US).
root_cause: This time, some partners may have received a few HTTP 500 errors due to a database issue, which has now been resolved.

issue: DNS issues with some providers.
root_cause: Some customers are experiencing connection issues to their Oplift instance due to a DNS issue with some providers.
solution: DNS issues (including those using OpenDNS) have cleared now some stale records have been purged.

issue: Elevated API Errors on AppGrid API service. Yesterday (2016-08-16) at the AppGrid API experienced a downtime lasting for 11 minutes, ending.
root_cause: The preliminary root cause analysis indicates that the problem comes from an issue in the load balancing mechanism in AWS (Amazon Web Services), which AppGrid relies function.

issue: Multiple Customers Impacted due to Upstream ISP.
root_cause: Multiple customers hosted in the Atlanta datacenter may be facing a service degradation due to an issue with one of the upstream internet providers.
solution: Connection has been successfully failed over to the second upstream provider, and all services have been restored.

issue: Issue in API Production Environment (US).

root_cause: Most Firefox add-ons stopped working around May 4th 2019 when a certificate expired. Firefox requires a valid certificate chain to prevent malware. About nine hours later, Mozilla pushed a privileged add-on that injected a valid certificate into Firefox's certificate store, creating a valid chain and unblocking add-ons. This disabled effectively all add-ons, about 15,000, and the resolution took approximately 15-21 hours for most users. Some user data was lost. Previously Mozilla posted about the technical details.
solution: Part of the reason for this misunderstanding was that in a previous incident we had disabled end-entity certificate checking, and this led to confusion about the status of intermediate certificate checking.

issue: By Marek Majkowski Reliability, Post Mortem, Mitigation, 1.1.1.1, DNS A Post Mortem on this Morning's Incident We would like to share more details with our customers and readers on the internet outages that occurred this morning and earlier in the week, and what we are doing to prevent these from happening again.
root_cause: Backwards time flow from tracking the 27th leap second on 2016-12-31T23:59:60Z caused the weighted round-robin selection of DNS resolvers (RRDNS) to panic and fail on some CNAME lookups. Go's time.Now was incorrectly assumed to be monotonic; this injected negative values into calls to rand.Int63n, which panics in that case.
solution: The most affected machines were patched in 90 minutes and the fix was rolled out worldwide by 0645. Discuss on Twitter Discuss on Hacker News Discuss on Reddit DNS Post Mortem RRDNS Bugs Reliability Follow on Twitter John Graham-Cumming | @jgrahamc Cloudflare | Cloudflare Related Posts Today we mitigated 1.1.1.1 Cloudflare is protected from attacks by the Gatebot DDoS mitigation pipeline.

issue: Slow Performance. Since rendering a view on the Admin Site requires many database queries, this was most evident on the admin site as pages would be slow to render or only render partially.
root_cause: It took us a few hours to figure out and solve the root cause, so the right thing to do is let you know what was going on behind the scenes. The Background Despite going out of our way to way to make FieldClock appear simple, there’s a lot going on under the surface.

issue: Degraded Performance of Editor for Web and Term Base Components. issue: DeafBeef NFTs not showing.

issue: Once the foreign key migration was successful, the internal engineering teams then worked to slowly remove token records stored in our cache layer that were considered invalid.
root_cause: This incident was caused when a foreign key for scoped tokens exceeded max INT32, which resulted in high failure rates for GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages.
solution: We mitigated this with a long-running schema migration to change the foreign key to INT64. After these cached records were removed, newly created API tokens were able to generate new records and API calls resumed working as expected.

issue: Workspot Control Email Services Incident.
root_cause: Starting May 19th, it was discovered that emails were not being delivered from the Workspot service due to a security update at our email provider.
solution: At Workspot Control Service was restarted to enable the security update from our email provider.

issue: Impact to O365 migrations when using Impersonation permissions.
root_cause: Microsoft have provided an update that the fix for this issue is in the process of being deployed to affected tenants at this time.
solution: All indications show that the deployment of the fix has been completed by Microsoft and that this issue has been resolved for our customers. We have had reports where this has been deployed to tenants already and has resolved the issue.

issue: Smart AC Control connectivity issue.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in North American Region – Web User Interface. at approximately Pacific, the xMatters monitoring tools alerted Customer Support to an issue where the web user interface was unresponsive or exhibiting slow performance.

The team then manually cleared the cache and restarted the web user interface service, confirming that it had resumed normal operation.

issue: Box might show devices as offline even though they were not. And this led to slower events processing, consequently causing devices’ offline connection status in the Box, REST API, and other services.

issue: Summary of AWS Direct Connect Event in the Tokyo (AP-NORTHEAST-1) Region. Engineers attempted several mitigations, such as resetting failed devices and slowly bringing them back into service, but the failures continued and the engineers were unable to maintain adequate healthy capacity to fully mitigate the customer impact.
root_cause: This was caused by the failure of a subset of network devices on one of the network layers along the network path from Direct Connect edge locations to the Datacenter network in the Tokyo Region, where customers’ Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) reside.
solution: While these devices were not correctly forwarding traffic, they were not being removed from the network through the normal automated processes that monitor and remove failed network devices. Customers started reporting recovery to their applications by JST and by JST affected networking devices were restored to a stable operational state and the Direct Connect service returned to normal operations.

issue: DNS lookup failures. Summary On Thursday, from approximately until our US commercial and government hosting environments both experienced a service interruption related to a configuration error in the service we use to manage our domain name and DNSSEC configuration, GoDaddy.
root_cause: Root Cause We confirmed with GoDaddy support that they experienced a failure in their managed DNSSEC service that caused some of the regular updates to DNSSEC records to not succeed.
solution: Approximately we cleared the interruption by manually resetting the state on our DNSSEC configuration, and this resulted in queries succeeding across all our monitoring regions within minutes. We observed that the outcome of this failure was that one of RRSIG signing key used to sign the DNSKEY records for the achieveit.com domain was not properly rotated and thus expired September.

issue: Degraded Performance of the File Processing Component. issue: Shipping addresses with special characters (accents, umlauts, etc) failing to create orders.

issue: 502 Errors. This resulted in the 502 errors seen, and other disruption to the Wordpress Cluster.

solution: In order to resolve this, we shutdown the database cluster, cleared all open connections held through our webservers and then brought the database cluster up one node at a time, using the most up to date node to prevent data loss.

issue: Survey Sending Issues in German Data Center.

issue: Notifications - Degraded performance.

issue: Download API Outage. The download outage experienced today is now closed.

issue: Encompass Mobile Sync Issues: Sync failing for some users. Overview: MST (1 hours, 50 minutes) on 4/25/2022, the system handheld sync for all versions were 10-100x slower, leading to syncs failing from a timeout.

issue: SecurID Service Incident (NA Region) - Degraded Authentications. authentication services hosted in the North American region were degraded for 2 hours and 45 minutes (from ET to ET).

issue: SignRequest reminders not delivered.

issue: As CPU utilization on the database continued to rise, the Container registry began responding to requests with increased latency, followed by an internal server error for a percentage of requests.
root_cause: This increased CPU activity was due to a high volume of the “Put Manifest” command. The reason for the CPU utilization was that the throttling criteria configured at the API side for this command was too permissive, and a database query was found to be non-performant under that degree of scale.
solution: In order to limit impact we throttled the requests from all organizations/users and to restore normal operation, we had to reset our database state by restarting our front-end servers and then the database.

issue: JVM Garbage collection on one of the API Servers had gone awry.
root_cause: One of the API Servers had gotten into an impaired state, due to an issue with Java Garbage collection. We have terminated the offending server error rates are back at normal.

issue: Dedicated VPC customers connecting to metadata database in AWS Oregon us-west-2. During this time, these projects experienced a period of downtime.

issue: Increased 502 responses to our Core API.
root_cause: We believe this is due to a recently introduced piece of code that is consuming more memory than it should be and are working on a fix.

issue: Queue delay affecting CDN purges and emails.
root_cause: Summary PyPI initially experienced delays in features which used a centralized task queue (such as purging the CDN cache and sending emails) due to a poorly performing task type.
solution: On Sun, 26 Jun 2022 PyPI admins deployed an unrelated change which replaced the JSON serializer used by PyPI from the standard library JSON serializer to a third-party JSON serializer, with benchmarks indicating that this would result in a 6x savings on time to serialize JSON, and thus a significant savings on response time for PyPI’s various JSON-rendering endpoints. PyPI admins deployed the first change that disabled the 2FA metrics task, which resulted in stopping additional long-running queries from being created.

issue: Incident - REST API (SDK) applet upload and login endpoints failing with 500 response code. Date 2022-06-29 Authors Michael Zabka, CTO Michal Artazov, DevOps Lead Summary signageOS Trial and Free-tier customers experienced increased traffic on some REST API endpoints between -.

issue: Errors when trying to check users. Without a cache storage, Dangerous Discord would not work at all, and the reason is that the cache stores all user information such as username and avatar.

issue: Slow and failing Agent chart data responses. Users with nightly versions of the Netdata Agent are experiencing slow responses between Cloud and Agent, resulting in failing or slow charts in their Cloud dashboards.
root_cause: In the mean time we've also found the true cause: the Agent was not properly processing incoming commands in the MQTT5 implementation, due to a bug in how the parser interacted with the buffer of incoming data.
solution: Reverting the default away from MQTT5 removed the immediate issue, and most Agents on the nightlies are now on the latest (v1.35.0-104-nightly). Latest, corrected version is v1.35.0-104-nightly.

issue: Unable to download files from Teamleader Focus in Google Chrome and Firefox.

issue: Major Core API outage. Upon investigation it became evident that an unexpected increase in load on the PostgreSQL database that serves our Core API was causing our application to struggle to serve some requests and we saw increased latency on those that were being served.
root_cause: The compounding factor was due to a bug in our Node client regarding request timeouts. The Node client takes an argument of requestTimeoutSeconds on instantiation, however, it passes this directly into the call to the Node Fetch’s library fetch function which expects the timeout to be passed in milliseconds.

issue: This incident occurred in August but was left out of the August report because it did not result in a widespread outage.

Seesaw’s swift response to this attack included the following steps: - As we resolved the issue, we completely disabled our messaging feature to ensure no one else saw the inappropriate message.

Restored access to the graphcdn.app domain, which resolved the issue for any services using graphcdn.app (The time those services were available again varied slightly depending on DNS propagation.) - Marked the incident resolved.

issue: Server outtage. 🙅‍♀️ Fault Once the mentioned code was deployed to our application servers, it slowly increased the used memory of the Redis instance over a period of three weeks.
root_cause: We immediately started investigating the issue and found that our main Redis instance, which handles asynchronous job processing and caching, had run out of available memory, and therefore all calls to Redis were failing.
solution: The review of the code, we failed to notice a missing flag in our Redis queueing code, which removed completed jobs from Redis. After ~20 minutes AWS was able to provision the resized instance, which restored our API availability.

issue: Issues connecting to calls.

issue: Based on learnings from this incident, we are evaluating expanding our regional redundancy and have started making architectural changes to better handle temporary regional and datacenter outages, including more regularly exercising our failover capabilities.

solution: Swapcard confirmed that the update was completed and capacity restored to pre-incident levels, ensuring that the traffic was back to the pre-incident rate.

issue: Searches are running slowly. The rate of requests was high enough to slow down all requests related to search results within the pod’s zone (one out of three total).

solution: Why it happened: In a previous incident on (more details at two pods storing logs were temporarily removed from the pool of pods available for receiving and inserting new batches of logs into our data store. How we fixed it: We removed the pod from the pool available for receiving and inserting new batches of logs into our data store.

issue: Intermittent 404s downloading Node.js.
root_cause: The origin server for nodejs.org was being overloaded, and due to a recent configuration change, was now erroneously returning 404 responses for valid files when it was overloaded and couldn't read them from its disk.
solution: The Incident Starting on March 15th and going through to March 17th (with much of the issue being mitigated on the 16th), users were receiving intermittent 404 responses when trying to download Node.js from nodejs.org, or even accessing parts of the website. A build script bug caused by the recent migration of the website to Next.js resulted in the site being rebuilt and the entire Cloudflare cache being purged every five minutes, sending an abnormally high number of requests to the origin server and putting it under excessive load.

issue: Increased Latency and Reduced Availability in the US, EU, and Global Region Groups. Between January 9th and January 13th, users in our US, EU, and Global Region Groups experienced multiple periods of increased latency and reduced availability.
root_cause: The issue was caused by a series of DDoS attacks that were targeted at a set of our customers, resulting in extreme waves of traffic to Fauna, each of which were many orders of magnitude above our baseline traffic patterns.
solution: After initial investigation, engineers realized that despite the fact that the requests were being throttled and sent a 429 response at the compute layer due to exceeding throughput limits, routing nodes were still experiencing resource starvation due to the number of connections being held and resources associated with request handling being kept in memory. Engineers identified and blocked offending accounts, causing the compute layer to short circuit the normal request handling process and return 410 responses for requests from those accounts, which shortened the time that each connection wa.

solution: The affected resource was restarted and the errors cleared.

issue: We're experiencing StormApi issues. Incident Norce Storm Monday Feb 5th 2024 During the evening of Monday the 5th primarily StormApi started to suffer from degraded performance at ca.
root_cause: Root cause The root cause of the problem was a high load on certain endpoints which requires extensive use of azure resources (depending on setup in Norce Storm) which accumulated and eventually requests "stacked up" and the compute nodes ran out of sockets/resources and performance dropped, certain requests timed out or received an error.
solution: Actions during the incident To handle the problem while investigating the root cause, we scaled up compute nodes for StormApi by a factor of x2, that helped at least marginally, but did not provide a satisfactory service level.

issue: Adding new database or executing SQL statement in Cloud UniversalSQL Editor takes forever.
root_cause: The issues were caused by changes to further tighten security. An issue has been identified that leads adding a new database or executing an SQL statement in Cloud UniversalSQL Editor to take forever.

issue: Incident with GitHub PR Checks.
root_cause: This incident resulted from a failure in a critical queue responding to status checks, causing some status checks to get ‘stuck’.
solution: We resolved the specific issue that affected our queues and upgraded our queueing system configuration so that such errors won't happen again.

issue: Typeform Webhooks, Integrations and Follow-ups - Delivery delayed. We are working on resolving an interruption impacting our Webhooks, Integrations, and Follow-ups with high priority.
root_cause: Syncing results to Google Sheets may experience delays due to the substantial volume of data being processed. Our systems are performing optimally, with webhooks, Follow-Ups, and integrations all functioning as expected.
solution: A fix has been deployed, and we will continue to update users on the progress.

issue: Mails service interruption. Between the hours of 6 AM and 2 PM today, Thursday 8 February, our notification service via email was interrupted.
root_cause: The issue was triggered by an attack on our servers that had no consequence on the security of customer accounts and data.
solution: We will send an additional update when the creation of user accounts is fully restored.

issue: Maintenance operations in Belgium, Europe (europe-west1) region.
root_cause: New trial cluster creation is temporary disabled due to a maintenance operation only in the Belgium region. Pre-existing clusters in that region are unaffected.
solution: New trial cluster creation has been re-enabled in Belgium region.

issue: Circle is unresponsive or offline. until on some servers may have experienced increased latency or the bot appearing offline.
root_cause: This was caused by a network routing error on the node Circle (regular) is hosted.
solution: On Feb 9, all sessions to Discord were invalidated and systems were fully operational.

issue: Help Desk Ticketing System Outage.
root_cause: The root cause was due to a change in profile access that inadvertently removed the ability to see team queues entirely.

issue: Product API stability issues.
root_cause: We tried a few actions that temporarily restored access but ultimately we did not know the root cause yet at this point and the feature soon reverted to its degraded status.

issue: Tilt Platform Dashboard displaying blank and users unable to log in.
root_cause: Time To Resolution: 20 minutes Root Cause: Long running database query that monopolized database resources. Resolution: Optimized queries to prevent further issues.

issue: Degraded Performance for Users in the Deutsche Telekom Network. However, our MTN Media Cloud, hosted separately on mtnmedia.cloud, is still experiencing slower loading times.
root_cause: This problem is due to a routing conflict between Deutsche Telekom (DTAG) and Cloudflare, a major internet infrastructure provider.

issue: Issue with Email Automations.
root_cause: The system overseeing automations for purchase expiration scheduled emails was not operating as expected due to an increased data load.
solution: Purchase Expiration emails have been temporarily restored to their default settings using the standard 1 and 7 day interval. For accounts that had previously disabled Purchase Expiration emails, these emails will remain disabled.

issue: Incident with Entitle Application. This disruption lasted for a total of 31 minutes.
root_cause: The root cause of the incident was identified as a misconfiguration in the database migration script, which occurred during a routine system update.

issue: S1 - TEEM Services unavailable. Type of Event: Outage Services/Modules impacted: All production.
root_cause: Teem by Eptura detailed Root Cause Analysis | 2/12/2024 S1 – Inability to Access Teem We are truly grateful for your continued support and loyalty. Description: On Monday, around MST both internal and external customers experienced an inability to access Teem.
solution: Investigation continues the issue has been resolved and we have moved Virtual Machines to allow hosting for our database.

issue: Trello is slow or unavailable. 13, 2024, Trello experienced severely degraded performance appearing as a full or partial outage to Atlassian customers.
root_cause: The root cause of the incident was identified as a compression change in our database deployed approximately 11 hours earlier during a low-traffic period.
solution: The incident was detected by our monitoring system was mitigated by reverting the compression change and restarting components of our database system.

issue: Service Disruptions Affecting Atlassian Products. Summary Atlassian customers on the following cloud products encountered a service disruption: Access, Atlas, Atlassian Analytics, Bitbucket, Compass, Confluence, Ecosystem apps, Jira Service Management, Jira Software, Jira Work Management, Jira Product Discovery, Opsgenie, StatusPage, and Trello.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE As part of a security and compliance uplift, we had scheduled the deletion of unused and legacy domain names that were being used for internal service-to-service connections.

issue: Intermittent timeouts on API endpoints.
root_cause: We believe this issue is being caused by excess database load related to a bug fix deployed earlier today around download counting.

issue: Network connectivity to Storm Iver is down. We will ensure that we are informed of potential maintenance downtime to be able to inform our customers as well through statuspage.
root_cause: The incident was caused by a network maintenance task by our network provider that inadvertantly caused a downtime of ca 6 minutes.
solution: The network issue have been identified by our network provider and connectivity have been restored.

issue: Elevated error rate in the Application for EU region.
root_cause: We observed high rate of errors for the Eightfold Application in the EU region.

issue: Searches impacted | CINC - 55235 ( Degraded Performance ).
root_cause: Please be aware, once the issue will be confirmed as resolved the Root Cause Messaging will be shared accordingly. Splunk has identified the issue causing memory growth on the indexers.

issue: Telemetry degradation. It should work as a standalone instance when all secondary replicas are down or unavailable.
root_cause: Trigger PagerDuty - Grafana Alerts of MongoDB Telemetry 0, Replication lag Detection - immediately after the incident started Root Causes Page faults - probably on HW of MongoDB Telemetry instances Remediation Increase IOPS on MongoDB Telemetry Data disks to 6000 iops Change the settings of MongoDB to HA.

issue: Degraded Performance of the DRACOON Cloud.
root_cause: Why Did This Happen: The incident occurred as a result of a race condition, a scenario where multiple threads or processes compete for shared resources in an unpredictable manner.
solution: What We Can Do to Improve: To prevent similar incidents in the future, we have implemented several proactive measures aimed at enhancing system resilience and stability.

issue: Users unable to access Kontent.ai. Content Production (both via user interface and MAPI) performance for projects in the US data center is still severely degraded.
root_cause: The performance challenges experienced in our US data center were caused by a bug within Microsoft's Azure Cosmos DB SDK, which is currently a top priority for resolution on their side.
solution: We have applied a fix for the US data center, and projects are continuously returning to normal.

issue: Issues loading app.cloudcannon.com.
root_cause: App.cloudcannon.com is down due to a DDOS on the servers, we are working to mitigate the attack.

issue: Degraded Performance of DRACOON Cloud.
root_cause: The performance of our DRACOON Cloud was degraded for some customers due to an extraordinary load situation on one component.
solution: Our auto-healing configuration therefore restarted the affected/stuck transactions which cleared the situation (the transaction backlog) within a couple of minutes. An automated process restarted some stuck teansactions, so they could be processed as planned.

issue: Campus Networking Issue. A widespread networking outage is currently impacting many services on campus.
root_cause: A power outage was the root cause of this morning's networking issues.
solution: Power has been restored and services are coming back online.

issue: DNS resolving issues within instances.
root_cause: The cause of this issue was a defective transfer of DNS zone guests.core.fuga.cloud from our primary to our secondary name servers.
solution: Fixing the defective zone resolved the issue.

issue: Reports: Zero Search Results & Product Recommendations Report.
root_cause: However, due to the large volume of data involved (in the terabyte realm), we anticipate that this process will take several more days.
solution: We received an update from the Engineering team that the Zero Search Results report has been restored through 2/24 so far. Our engineering team has given us an update and they expect reports to be fully restored by the end of the week.

issue: Sites running on MySQL 4 are inaccessible. Summary: On February 26th, 2024 at MST, the MySQL 4 server experienced an outage, causing customers to be unable to access their ECP site.
root_cause: Cause of the Issue: The outage was caused by an issue with the deletion of a large amount of data on a site, which cascaded into locking of database tables and the server and ultimately required we restart the database.
solution: The issue was identified and resolved by MST. Resolution: The issue was resolved immediately by killing the offending queries and clearing up some of the data being deleted, in addition to restarting the server.

issue: Heartbeat issue with Google SAS. In summary, the Google SAS server was operating as expected and the outage was due to some maintenance made on the test servers last night which were mistakenly replicated to our live servers.
root_cause: The heartbeat errors due to 103 response code are due to the grant IDs being invalid. However, the grant IDs were never changed and the response codes are only found after the CPAS event this morning.
solution: Wait for CBSDs to indicate the SAS is disabled.

issue: Issue with Bolt’s embed.js script in Sandbox.
root_cause: A Bolt deployment introduced an error to the Sandbox version of embed.js. This error would have impacted shopper login, credit card validation, and Bolt account-related testing in the sandbox.

issue: Litify Inbox is Currently Down.
root_cause: We believe the cause of this issue has been identified and traced back to a change from Microsoft.

issue: Intermittent Visual Issues with Non-Chromium Browsers. The issue with visual elements not working as expected on non-chromium browsers has been resolved.
root_cause: The internal site caching tool had a faulty cache string caused by a recent update. If users are still experiencing issues, please clear your browser cache and cookies.

issue: Canned Responses: problems with loading data in US region.
root_cause: The issue has been identified by Atlassian and they are now investigating the root cause. Seems like there an issue with Jira API in US region and because of this Canned Responses cannot work properly.
solution: The Jira incident that caused issues with Canned Responses is now resolved by Atlassian.

issue: Issue Events: integration interrupted service.
root_cause: Issue Events is fully operational now The issue has been identified by Atlassian: Seems like there is an issue with Jira API and because of this Issue Events cannot work properly (Side panel view is not loading).
solution: The Jira incident that caused issues with Issue Events is now resolved by Atlassian.

issue: Banner Admin Pages: Issues Following Upgrades.
root_cause: Ellucian has identified a defect and has provided a patch. Admin pages will be unavailable for approximately 5 minutes while this work is performed.

issue: Queens Tower and Connected sites offline.
root_cause: An engineer has attended site and discovered that some of the equipment had some power issues. Our initial diagnostics indicate a potential issue with third-party equipment in the main cabinet at Queens Tower.

issue: Partial Outage of Storage (Up- and Download).
root_cause: One of our automated quality checks introduced a too restrictive policy without context, leading to a software change which resulted in non-working up- and downloads for hybrid customers.
solution: In this post-mortem, we want to share the details of what happened, why it happened, what we did to resolve it, and what we will do to prevent similar incidents in the future. We are committed to ensuring the stability and reliability of our services and will continue to take proactive measures to prevent similar incidents from happening in the future.

issue: Leap year miscalculation possibilities.
root_cause: This appears to be due to the leap year not being taken into consideration.

issue: Frontend slowdowns and slow response times in the POS/admins.
root_cause: We’ve applied a change to a third party middle ware that appears to have been accidentally misconfigured which was leading to higher than normal response times.

issue: Failures for Presence Webhooks.
root_cause: Problem Description, Impact, and Resolution we observed the Presence service started experiencing missed Presence webhook calls.
solution: We rolled back the migration for all customers in case the issue was broader and created a status page for transparency.

issue: Website unavailable. The website is available again, but visitors might experience degraded performance.
root_cause: It seems to issue persisted after the initial outage due to an error with the SVCB record, which caused a GET error solely for the URL including the ‘www.’ subdomain. Requests made to the root were temporarily not redirected to www.cloudfrl.com in an effort to lower the potential impact.

issue: Delivery REST API items feed endpoint - older continuation tokens causing request failures.
root_cause: Because of the newly released code, users might encounter failed requests for the Delivery REST API items feed endpoint when using older continuation tokens (created before the release, roughly 3 hours ago).

issue: Message queue causing significant delays.
root_cause: Root cause not yet identified Incident is ongoing and we are restoring normal operations and monitoring the performance currently.

issue: Avalor platform is not accessible.
root_cause: We found out that one of our load balancers was malfunction. Dear Customers, We're currently facing connectivity issues on our platform for the past 10 minutes.

issue: Kami Backend Outage. At Pacific Time, we've seen that API recover, and our error rates have decreased.
root_cause: This outage did appear to be caused by an outage by Google SSO APIs. We've identified our outage is being caused by Google SSO backend API was down.

issue: Unified Communications Email Performance Issue.
root_cause: Our system administrators have identified and addressed the root cause of the problem. The issue was traced back to a misconfiguration during a update.

issue: US accounts - Editor/Insights/Console is down - Partial Workstation and ActionBot outage. After urgent investigation by the WalkMe engineering team, and in order to avoid further disruption, a set of recovery steps was performed on the databases and load balancers.
root_cause: Root Cause Analysis A new product configuration caused some of our underlying services to enter an unstable state.

issue: Partial Outage Due to Unexpected Traffic Peak. The incident lasted for 2 minutes and 36 seconds, disrupting service availability for some of our users.
root_cause: Our systems experienced a partial outage due to an unexpected surge in requests, which overwhelmed our servers.

issue: Transaction Processing Issues. There are very small subset of our Merchants that are still experiencing processing issues due to yesterday's DNS outage.
root_cause: It appears that the transaction processing issues are due to a widespread issue affecting multiple Internet Service Providers.

issue: MARA Alert Importing and Reporting Incident. During the data import process, a disruption occurred in the communication between these systems, leading to the failure of proper alert importing and generation within MARA.
root_cause: Our team swiftly identified and resolved the root cause of the issue. The problem stemmed from a synchronization issue between our database due to recent downstream updates.
solution: As of 08.03.2024, the incident has been mitigated, and we are actively working to process and import all missed alerts into the system.

issue: INC0050996 - APEX Newbury - Device reloaded.
root_cause: The vendor has reviewed all the output that was submitted to them and concluded that the root cause of this device reload was down to a known software defect.

issue: Bloomreach Cloud - Operational Issues with Content PaaS clusters. Dear Customer, Our internal monitoring is reporting unavailability of nodes on multiple clusters.
root_cause: The root cause has been identified: a 3rd party tool was upgraded and it introduced a bug that caused networking issue on the nodes of several clusters.
solution: Dear Customer, A fix has been rolled out and the team is monitoring the situation.

issue: Internet Outage. Unfortunately, both of our providers experienced a service outage simultaneously, resulting in a significant service disruption.
root_cause: Our secondary backup provider experienced an unplanned fiber cut resulting in the internet service interruption due to the primary provider’s routine maintenance issues.
solution: Due to unforeseen issues, this maintenance turned into an outage and service was not restored. Crews worked to fix the fiber cut and service was restored.

issue: History lag and degraded performance on certain Horizon endpoints.
root_cause: We've identified a high CPU utilization on SDF Horizon nodes due to increased request load that saturated DB connections.

issue: S2 - O365 SSO Logging Issues. At around a fire alarm is pulled by Jared Collins Teem Support Manager Type of Event: Outage Services/Modules impacted: SSO/Logging.
root_cause: Teem by Eptura detailed Root Cause Analysis | 3/11/2024 S2 – O365 SSO Login Issues We are truly grateful for your continued support and loyalty. Description: (The Incident is logged in MST) On Monday on Monday March 11th Internal Teem members and customers started experiencing issues with logging into the Teem application via O365.

issue: Notification of new incident: Performance degradation, device connectivity issues: SG Deployment. The general tenant UI would have also been slow or unresponsive.
root_cause: Scope of Impact Singapore Deployment Incident Start Date and Time 11 March 2024 Incident End Date and Time 11 March 2024 Root Cause Following an investigation with Microsoft it was confirmed that the uniFLOW Online Cloud Services were located on a physical node which was experiencing faulted disk issues.
solution: User Impact Devices switched to emergency mode, slow response or timeouts on printing and scanning actions.

issue: Downtime Transactional Email API.
root_cause: The issue was identified to be caused by an error in configuration related to an update. A fix is being deployed and the transactional API full availability should resume shortly.
solution: Normal traffic for Transactional Email API was restored.

issue: Mainnet token associate issue.
root_cause: The MAX_ENTITIES_IN_PRICE_REGIME_HAVE_BEEN_CREATED error was caused by the increased network usage and adoption we’re seeing from multiple applications.
solution: Although the network capacity was increased recently with the “Data on Disk” improvements, the token associations limit was not adjusted to match this increased capacity. A fix has been rolled out and we are monitoring its impact The issue has been identified and a fix is being implemented.

issue: Some customers are experiencing issues logging into Vivantio.
root_cause: Cause: After investigation by the Vivantio engineering team, the cause of the issue was determined to be due to a short-lived database outage that stopped the validation service from working.
solution: Resolution: Our engineers performed an investigation into the issue and once the root cause was established, they were able to restart the service which corrected the issue.

issue: Some recordings from web projects might not be replayable.
root_cause: The root cause was AWS load balancer controller failure, which we have fixed in coordination with AWS support.

issue: Delays Reporting Certain Opening Execution Messages.
root_cause: Due to a technical issue at one of DriveWealth's liquidity partners, DriveWealth experienced delays reporting a limited number of opening execution trade reports to certain partners.

issue: System severely degraded: app admin temporarily unavailable. Mar 19, our app was severely degraded, temporarily inaccessible for 15 minutes.
root_cause: The root cause was due to a new released feature consuming too much server resources, causing out of memory issues.

issue: Degraded Performance of the Upload Feature.
root_cause: The update introduced an edge case, which resulted in some uploads occasionally getting delayed for a small amount of our customers. Our incident response team quickly identified the underlying issue and resolved it for the affected component.
solution: In this post-mortem, we want to share the details of what happened, why it happened, what we did to resolve it, and what we will do to prevent similar incidents in the future.
