issue: FACEIT Clipping is currently offline.
root_cause: Due to a recent change in polices and enforcement around the FACEIT API we are unable to download your demos from FACEIT.

issue: Database congestion resulting in partial outage and extended response times. This caused a partial outage, but was affecting all services.
root_cause: The primary database was congested with a huge spike in requests due to some misconfiguration.

issue: Performance issues and timeouts.
root_cause: The problem was caused by a database lock, we continue to work with the root cause of the problem but the incident is deemed to be over and is closed.

issue: Issue Discovered - Service disruption in All Regions – Mobile App (Android only). Certificate transparency is an important part of the mobile app's end-to-end security and we are currently testing mitigation strategies to ensure they will not cause any disruption of this feature.
root_cause: The problem appears to have stemmed from a third-party conflict: the way the certificate transparency library handles updates from the Google log list conflicts with its own concurrency and job cancellation.
solution: The issue has been resolved, and no app update is required at this time. The issue has been resolved; no app update is required.

issue: Dynamic Imaging Performance Issues. Disabling this modification resolved the service disruption.
root_cause: Upon further analysis, we discovered that it stemmed from a recent change pushed out by Cloudflare to all environments. Root Causes: Cloudflare, a third-party supplier, implemented a modification to HTTP/2, which took effect in our environment by default.

issue: EXpurgate.Inhouse and eXpurgate.Cloud - Datacenter Outage. Detection performance is still degraded due to issue in the backend that we are working.
root_cause: Due to the outage we are unable to update the detection database, so the quality of the detection is still degraded.

issue: Australian Users Only - Phone Numbers Blocked.
root_cause: AUSTRALIAN USERS ONLY Due to a misuse of the Kalix platform to send SMS spam to outside accounts, our Australian-based numbers have been temporarily locked to prevent further spam being sent out by our provider.
solution: The Australian phone numbers have been restored and configured so all SMS functionality should be working as usual.

issue: Intermittent 503 responses from SDK API. This can lead to initialization timeouts for SDKs initializing from an empty cache.
root_cause: Our team detected the root cause for this issue in a high amount of variants for cached resources being created in certain scenarios.
solution: This issue has been resolved and all our systems are healthy. All indicators are currently healthy and validate that the fix has effectively mitigated the issue.

issue: Some paginated queries in Forge hosted storage kept repeating the last page.
root_cause: Activating changes recently made to the query cursors for paginated queries introduced a bug that impacted some apps.
solution: Incident was resolved and impact ended The impact of this incident has been completely mitigated and our monitoring tools confirm that query operations are back to the pre-incident behaviour.

issue: Slow SAAS Builds due to AWS Issue.
root_cause: We are currently seeing an impact on builds and services on our SAAS platform due to an API error currently impacting provisioning new nodes in US-EAST-1.

issue: Partial Outage. Later, we experienced degraded database performance as a residual effect of the main issue.
root_cause: Root Cause We have finished investigating our database infrastructure and codebase.
solution: Upon investigating, we applied the needed fixes and restarted all backend application services, which restored their operations.

issue: Degraded Happeo Performance. During the first hours of the incident, Happeo became unavailable at times, a situation that was controlled by our Engineering team by providing extra capacity to our cloud resources.
root_cause: Starting 26.03.2024 at around we have detected a bug in the Google infrastructure we use to perform data replication within the microservices that power Happeo different features.
solution: We have resolved the issue originating from Google and all services should be running as expected again.

issue: Rutter Link infrastructure provider outage.
root_cause: Our infrastructure provider for Rutter Link is experiencing an outage, so we have re-routed requests to a backup provider.

issue: Dashboard Inaccessible. Overview Between ET and ET the Admiral Dashboard was inaccessible and customers saw an error message.
root_cause: Root Cause Analysis A misbehaving service led to instability across multiple servers that host the Dashboard.
solution: All of these issues were simultaneously corrected.

issue: Inaccurate customer alerts generated. At approximately on Wednesday March 27th, some customers may have received alerts from the YugabyteDB Managed system indicating their clusters were offline.
root_cause: Most of these alerts were false positives due to an administrative issue in YugabyteDB Managed impacting management of database clusters running in AWS.
solution: Once the administrative issue was resolved, all management of those clusters returned to normal.

issue: Degraded performance for TrustedForm Certify on several sites.
root_cause: We will continue investigation on issues caused by the latest version of the script. Rolling back TrustedForm Script to 1.9.4 We've received issues from 3 clients that the TrustedForm Script has not been working properly since around 3p CT on March 27th.

issue: Unavailability of Box and REST API. Impact Box and API toggled between degraded performance to being completely unavailable.
root_cause: Root Causes Undetected accumulation of events in the Event Sourcing database over time leads to a gradual slowdown of future command processing.

issue: Service Disruption Notice: Pusher US2 Cluster. On Saturday March 30th from until Pusher channels experienced a partial outage and higher than usual latencies on our US2 cluster.
root_cause: The incident was triggered by a single, high volume customer sending requests that was causing an authentication error.
solution: This caused the rolling deployment to take much longer than expected, as it waited for old socket processes to be fully drained and terminated. After coordination with our cloud provider we were able to increase this limit, allowing the deployment to complete and the incident was resolved.

issue: Licensing Server unavailable.
root_cause: The Licensing server is unavailable, resulting in messages about licenses expiring soon or servers unable to connect.
solution: We have received feedback the issue was resolved.

issue: Interruption in service due to database failure.
root_cause: The Pulsara platform experienced a service outage due to a database failure from MDT until MDT.
solution: The Pulsara team was notified by internal monitoring systems about the issue and resolved the issue.

issue: Advanced Billing - Period of Processing Degradation. the Advanced Billing system encountered a period of degradation that affected a subset of subscriptions attempting to process during these periods of time.
root_cause: This period was caused by server connectivity problems, with the main result being that subscriptions encountered processing errors.
solution: These errors halt the processing of the subscription in order for our team to manually review and ensure the renewal is handled correctly when the processing error is cleared. Once the processing errors are cleared, the subscriptions will resume processing as normal and bill for their renewal.

issue: Outage of datacenter. They ensured us to improve their processes further to prevent any further complication like this outage to the best of their abilities.
root_cause: After noticing the incident, we immediately notified all our customers and began analyzing the root cause. Once we found out all our datacenter services went offline at the same time we immediately contacted our datacenter provider who confirmed the outage and their efforts to bring our systems back online asap.
solution: This caused our datacenter infrastructure to be suspended and therefore rendering it unusable at the time of the incident.

issue: Overnight System Processing Issue.
root_cause: Due to a systems processing issue, the generation of the beginning of day "Cash Available for Trading" and "Cash Available for Withdrawal" balances for the trade day is still ongoing.

issue: Appflow Builds and Live Updates - Service Interruption.
root_cause: While deploying one service to test the changes, one of the required secrets was not correctly migrated. This was not immediately detected as the service's successful responses were heavily cached.
solution: Once the required secret was migrated and caches were flushed, all service was restored. Remediation CI/CD pipeline is updated to check for missing / incorrectly migrated secrets and fail fast under this scenario.

issue: Service Dashboard view - minor issue fetching and displaying transaction data.
root_cause: Due to the recent clock change, the Dashboard view in the Admin Tool is displaying an error. This means transaction totals for the last 7 days are not being displayed on this page.

issue: Outage in ap-southeast-3. While responding to a few degraded hosts in AWS ap-southeast-3, we manually intervened to rotate in fresh instances.
root_cause: However, due to a misconfiguration new nodes were not scheduled on the new instances resulting in a 3 minute outage in that region.

issue: Database Environment Outage. No data was lost and the system has resumed normal operation after about 15 minutes of downtime.
root_cause: The hosting provider has clarified that the outage has effected networking infrastructure used by the database service, and the underlying issue is still ongoing.

issue: Explore Performance Issues.
root_cause: The root cause of the issue was an error in permissions management in our Manage product.
solution: Our monitoring and alerting worked as expected, and the team corrected the issue.

issue: Issues with Add to basket.
root_cause: A misconfigured TTL value was causing some cached data to expire prematurely. We have identified an issue with our add to basket API flow.

issue: Connectivity issue to various parts of the New Forest Enterprise Centre.
root_cause: This was caused by a power issue in part of the NFEC corridor which has been resolved by the centre management. This outage will be only impacting a sub-set of units within the building.

issue: Go live button in backstage session is not working. Executive Summary: We are issuing a post-mortem report regarding a backstage service disruption that affected Swapcard customers on Thursday, April 5th, 2024.
root_cause: A recent update introduced a modification whereby the recording process would terminate if it did not detect the session within the same cluster, leading to recorder failures.

issue: Issue with logging into Vivantio.
root_cause: The connectivity issues were caused by the deployment of front end gateways by Microsoft into that region.
solution: Microsoft mitigated the issue by stopping the active roll out deployment.

issue: Unable to raise support tickets via Support Portal. Summary Between April 05, some Atlassian customers were unable to submit support tickets via the Atlassian Support portal.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE The issue was caused by a change to a support form backend service resource file.
solution: The incident was detected within one minute by a customer and mitigated by rolling back the configuration change which put Atlassian Support form system into a known good state.

issue: Web request error rates peaked at 6% and API request error rates peaked at 10%, and over 100,000 GitHub Actions workflows failed to start.
root_cause: The root cause was traced to a change in the database load balancer, which caused connection failures to multiple critical databases in one of our three data centers.
solution: We resolved the incident by rolling back the change and have implemented new measures to detect similar problems earlier in the deployment pipeline to minimize user impact moving forward.

issue: We are investigating an issue with Teem. This incident has been closed, but our team is dedicated to closely monitoring future updates as they are released to ensure the best customer experience.

solution: Preventative Action: The Teem team was able to start a migration process and monitor it through successful completion and review with internal testing to ensure the issue was resolved for customers.

issue: Facebook Ads Integration - Extraction Job Failures.
root_cause: Our Facebook Ads integration was experiencing extraction job failures due to an issue with our Facebook app.
solution: The issue has been resolved and we have returned to normal operations.

issue: Airbridge dashboards and APIs.
root_cause: There was an issue with access to the Airbridge dashboard and most Airbridge APIs due to an unexpected failure that occurred during infrastructure operations.

issue: API/Dashboard/Applications back to normal. The cloud service provides safeguards during upgrades that automatically restores normal operations should a timeout exceed 5 minutes.

solution: Mitigation and resolution A few minutes before, our engineers tried to manually interrupt the process, but the option to cancel it was disabled by the vendor.

issue: Problems with connect.storm.io.
root_cause: The problem was caused by an import job which was restarted over and over again filling up the job queue and preventing new jobs to be started.
solution: The development team have identified the issue and is implementing a fix to prevent this edge case cause this problem.

issue: Continuation of incident: Microsoft Universal Print jobs failing: All deployments. User Impact Tenants making use of the Universal Print by Microsoft Extension would have had their Universal Print by Microsoft jobs not processed.
root_cause: As per the root cause only expired or expiring tenants were impacted. issue: Monitors partially unavailable. During the incident, our team communicated the outage through the status page and resolved it.

Cache invalidation job is restarted with fixed race condition Invalidation job is run for a second time, we see steady reduction of failed monitor runs towards zero.

issue: PyPI Simple Index Timing Out. PyPI experienced an outage which resulted in serving 500-level responses for certain requests, including requests to a subset of the Simple Repository API.
root_cause: While the actual details of this new functionality is unrelated, a misconfiguration of this new service resulted in views that depended on this service failing to successfully serve a response, which was missed by PyPI’s unit test suite and by manual testing of the feature branch.
solution: As a result of PyPI’s container orchestration and deployment service not explicitly supporting rollbacks, issues like this are generally resolved by introducing a new pull request which reverts the problematic commit, which in turn is merged and deployed. This migration could not be reverted simply by reverting the commit, as deployment would fail when it would attempt to bring the database up to date with the migration history, and find that the current migration version was no longer present.

issue: Breaking down OpenAI's outage: How to avoid a hidden DNS dependency in Kubernetes. Breaking down OpenAI's outage: How to avoid a hidden DNS dependency in Kubernetes Migrating production infrastructure?

issue: Searches are slow or down. Introduction This post-mortem details an incident where the SLI platform experienced significant service degradation impacting AWS CloudFront integrations.

issue: Post-incident review for 20th October 2025. Post-incident review for 20th October 2025 | Buildkite Resources / Blog / Post-incident review for 20th October 2025 On October 20th, 2025, customers experienced high latency and increased error rates across the majority of our services as a consequence of the major us-east-1 AWS outage.
root_cause: Buildkite customers started to experience latency and increasing error rates to varying degrees due to the increase in traffic.
solution: As a result, latency and error rates increased across all services and shards (particularly notifications and web traffic), we were able to shift some load from under-provisioned shards to an unused shard that we had scaled up for a load-testing experiment. Starting AWS allowed some compute to be provisioned at a severely limited rate.

issue: Cloudflare outage on | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Note: This post was updated to clarify the relationship of the internal WAF tool with the incident on Dec.
root_cause: A configuration change to disable an internal WAF testing tool propagated globally without a gradual rollout, triggering a Lua exception in the proxy's rulesets module that caused HTTP 500 errors for customers using the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset.
solution: The incident was resolved at (~25 minutes total impact), when all services were fully restored. The issue was identified shortly after the change was applied, and was reverted after which all traffic was served correctly.

issue: Cloudflare incident on | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Multiple Cloudflare services, including our R2 object storage, were unavailable for 59 minutes on Thursday.
root_cause: Human error during abuse remediation inadvertently disabled the R2 Gateway service instead of a specific endpoint, due to insufficient validation safeguards in admin tooling.
solution: This impacted less than 0.049% of all cacheable requests served during the incident window.User-facing requests for assets to sites with Cache Reserve did not observe failures as cache misses failed over to the origin. Time Event 2025-02-06 The R2 Gateway service is inadvertently disabled while responding to an abuse report.

issue: We’re deeply sorry for this incident and the disruption it may have caused to you or your users.
root_cause: Credential rotation, the R2 engineering team accidentally deployed new storage credentials to the default environment instead of production by omitting the --env production flag, causing the R2 Gateway to fail authentication once old credentials were removed.
solution: Once the root cause was identified and we realized we hadn’t deployed the new credentials to the production R2 Gateway service, we deployed the updated credentials and service availability was restored. User-facing requests for assets to sites with Cache Reserve did not observe failures as cache misses failed over to the origin.

issue: The degradation in performance was limited to traffic between Cloudflare and AWS us-east-1.
root_cause: A single customer's traffic surge from AWS us-east-1 saturated Cloudflare's peering links; AWS's BGP prefix withdrawals to mitigate congestion paradoxically rerouted traffic to already-strained alternate paths, compounded by a pre-existing half-capacity link failure and insufficient DCI capacity.
solution: Through close collaboration, we successfully alleviated the congestion and fully restored services for all affected customers. That caused a long tail of latency that may have impacted some customers, which is why you see the packet drops resolve before the customer latencies are restored.

issue: Cloudflare service outage | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Cloudflare suffered a significant service outage that affected a large set of our critical services, including Workers KV, WARP, Access, Gateway, Images, Stream, Workers AI, Turnstile and Challenges, AutoRAG, Zaraz, and parts of the Cloudflare Dashboard.
root_cause: Workers KV relies on a central data store for its source of truth; a failure of the third-party cloud provider backing that store caused a complete outage for cold reads and writes.
solution: Some providers may require a manual re-synchronization but most customers would have seen immediate service restoration once Access’ SCIM service was restored due to retry logic by the identity provider.Service authentication based logins (e.g. Workers KV removed a storage provider as we worked to re-architect KV’s backend, including migrating it to Cloudflare R2, to prevent data consistency issues (caused by the original data syncing architecture), and to improve support for data residency requirements.

Connectivity was restored around (local time) on October.

issue: Elevated Latency. Waiting for dequeue metrics to fall below 50% normal before we lift "degraded performance" rating.

issue: Maxio Platform 503 Error Access Issues.

issue: Accidental Deletion of Paid User Accounts.
root_cause: Root Cause The deletion logic did not account for users who had recently upgraded to a paid tier after the deletion lists were generated but before the deletion process was executed (a two week period).
solution: Unfortunately, due to a series of procedural oversights, this process resulted in the accidental deletion of about a dozen paid user accounts on the EU1 satellite that had upgraded their frozen account during the deletion procedure. This command mistakenly included some active, paid users who had upgraded their frozen account during the two week period after the deletion lists were generated and did not include robust safeguards to catch this sort of error.

issue: Disturbances in StomAPI. This caused a temporary disruption for some users.

issue: Trello is slow or unavailable. SUMMARY Atlassian customers using Trello may have experienced service interruptions.

issue: Playouts playing silence or stopping and starting randomly.
root_cause: The root cause is a degraded object storage on an external provider that we use as a second caching layer.

issue: How the, power outage in Portugal and Spain impacted Internet traffic and connectivity. root_cause: The conditions that cause the bug have been addressed and we're actively working on a permanent fix.

issue: Service Disruption Due To Power Outage.

solution: The issue has been resolved and all services are now operating normally.

issue: MVault Merge Tool Temporarily Disabled.

solution: There is a slow procession of devices falling offline, and we expect the pattern will continue until power is restored. Devices should reconnect once power is restored.

issue: Chinese characters an special characters not supported in email drafts.

solution: We reverted the recently made changes, and issue was resolved.

issue: Dynamic Content UI issues.

During a release, an update to the stack misconfigured, resulting in the UI not receiving confirmation of the successful publish.
solution: We are using this incident to review and strengthen our RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) model to prevent similar issues in future.

issue: Chili Cal Links displaying a "Something Went Wrong" page. Incident Overview Some users experienced intermittent failures when accessing ChiliCal scheduling links while others began experiencing no access to any booking links within their organization.

solution: We deployed a fix for this as an unrelated incident. This action immediately restored functionality for most users.

issue: Authentication Service Failures. The increased errors manifested as failed authentication for new attempts to the User Portal, SSO and other services.
root_cause: The issue was resolved at Root Cause: A state transition anomaly occurred during the credential rotation process for a database within our authentication infrastructure, resulting in connection failures by dependent services to that layer.
solution: The authentication service team was able to identify a failure with secondary credentials during the rotation and quickly failed back to valid secrets.

issue: Elevated Errors. On from - api.lob.com returned an elevated number of "Service Unavailable" 503 status code failures impacting most requests across all endpoints.
root_cause: This regression was caused by an update which has since been rolled back.

issue: Increased API and Dashboard response times.

issue: Webhook processing delayed.

issue: Active Directory User Status Impacted. This event disrupted user access and necessitated a password update for the affected users until JumpCloud successfully rectified their account status.

This resulted in the incorrect transformation of these fields, setting the password status of some external user accounts to "pending”.

issue: Incorrect content being received in push notifications.

issue: EMS Cloud access issue from Saudi Arabia.

issue: Runs failing with "flag provided but not defined: -var-file".

solution: RCA A fix was released to ensure.tfvars files are properly loaded during the init phase with for-each feature, that was introduced in the OpenTofu 1.9.0 version.

issue: Trello is slow or unavailable for some users. and p.m, some Atlassian customers using Trello were unable to view their boards or cards.

issue: Bitbucket has degraded performance. Customers may have seen intermittent errors or website latency during this time.

To prevent this type of incident from recurring, we are prioritizing the following improvement actions: Improve database request routing so that more reads go to read replicas instead of the write-primary database.

issue: WhatsApp Integration message delays Prod 1. ET - Slowdown of sending for WhatsApp messages.

root_cause: The root cause of the incident was related to instability in our underlying database hosting infrastructure.

solution: While the breaking change was reverted within a minute of deployment, there were still instances of cached data which extended the impact for a total of 4 minutes of partial service outage.

root_cause: However, due to the issue with cached responses being served incorrectly as either partial or empty data, this triggered the CSRF protection, as the data being returned was invalid.

issue: Cloudflare outage on | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Cloudflare experienced a service outage when a subset of customers who use Cloudflare’s Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) service saw their routes to the Internet withdrawn via Border Gateway Protocol (BGP).

issue: Natural disasters and government interference: examining Q2 2026’s major Internet disruption events. Natural disasters and government interference: examining Q2 2026’s major Internet disruption events | Cloudflare Blog Skip to content Like most infrastructure, the Internet's fragility is easy to overlook — as long as it's working.
root_cause: Here we will walk through the most significant Internet disruptions we observed in the second quarter of 2026, drawing on traffic data from Cloudflare Radar to show how each unfolded and what it meant for users on the ground.

root_cause: No further details on the root cause of the incident were publicly disclosed. TalkTalk (United Kingdom) On March 25, customers of UK broadband provider TalkTalk (AS13285) reported widespread service disruptions.

issue: Knowledge Graph as context for LLMs: demonstrating decisive RCA and faster production performance. Lookups slowed, the workers that run searches queued up behind them, and users saw slow searches.
root_cause: In one real incident we replayed 16 times each way, an agent with Knowledge Graph context found the correct root cause 15 times, compared with just once using raw telemetry alone. Along the way, we also uncovered some of the challenges that still stand in the way of reliable AI-assisted debugging, from chasing the wrong signals to confidently making things up and producing inconsistent answers.
solution: The servers holding it hit their 8 GB limit, were killed, restarted, filled up, and were killed again, roughly every 48 minutes. When we later replayed this incident as a controlled experiment, the runs without the Knowledge Graph blamed the query storm in 10 of 16 attempts, concluding the system was recovering on its own with nothing to fix.

issue: Incident Report: File Hosting Errors. flowchart TD Client(Client request) --> Edge{Fastly edge} Edge -->|package file| B2(B2: egress-free cache) Edge -->|everything else| ConveyorConveyor B2 -->|200 or 206| Response(Response to client) B2 -.->|404, timeout, or 5xx| Archive(S3: origin, fallback) Archive --> Response Conveyor --> Response That fallback path only works if the edge notices B.
root_cause: A canary deployment inside Fastly's network had triggered a misconfiguration at one cache node, causing Fastly's routing layer to return 502 responses for traffic reaching the affected cache node.

issue: Temporary eCommerce Rate Limit.
root_cause: Due to a dramatic increase in eCommerce traffic, we have temporarily implemented a rate limiting Captcha that customers may encounter when browsing your website; once they have completed the Captcha they should be able to continue to browse without interruption for a period of time.

issue: Reduced performance / errors in Autify Nexus Cloud.
root_cause: We've identified and mitigated the root cause of the database performance issue in Autify Nexus.

issue: Unable to reach bitbucket site. Summary Atlassian customers using Bitbucket Cloud could not load the dashboard landing page.
root_cause: ROOT CAUSE The event was caused by an unexpected load on a public API.
solution: The incident was detected within three minutes by automated monitoring systems and mitigated by introducing stricter limits on the API for certain traffic, while taking manual actions on the impacted database, restoring Bitbucket to a healthy state.

issue: Issues with Multiple Box Services. On January 7th, 2026, some customers experienced elevated errors and timeouts across multiple Box experiences, including Login, Uploads/Downloads, Box Notes, and the Public API.
root_cause: These issues were caused by a series of changes that triggered a request storm that overloaded our caching fleet.
solution: Unfortunately, one critical code path that had been migrated to a newer infrastructure had a more aggressive retry policy than the old one. To resume normal operations, we deprioritized some background traffic to increase the capacity of our cache system, and rolled back the changes that were causing the elevated traffic.

issue: Issues authenticating with Azure DevOps in Appflow.
root_cause: The issue was caused by the expiration of our Azure DevOps OAuth client secret, which had been valid for 5 years since its creation in January 2021.

issue: Severe service disruption across the platform in EU. As remedies to that incident we: immediately put in place alerting on other tables experiencing similar growth across our systems; scheduled proactive table migrations to avoid other similar disruptions of service.
root_cause: Surge of retry requests from multiple customers identified as root cause; infrastructure scaled up.
solution: As part of those scheduled migrations, during 2025, we migrated multiple tables that store information about Documents. On the 7th, as predicted by our monitoring, another primary key which had already been migrated, went over the former maximum limit.

issue: AWS Outage. As services come back online there may be slower processing times.
root_cause: Currently it appears that the AWS outage may be caused by an internet service provider backbone limiting the scope to certain stores; we are seeing successful transactions process.

issue: Issues with Logins, Notes and API.
root_cause: US Pacific time, we observed an issue impacting Logins, Notes and API.

root_cause: ROOT CAUSE A change was introduced that caused cross-region traffic routing for customers instead of routing to the same region.

issue: Search and Page Load Issues.
root_cause: We'll publish a brief post-mortem in the next 48 hours once the root cause is confirmed, but performance seems to be normal once again.

issue: Insights ingestion delayed.

issue: Platform: All Regions - Unable to launch PRA session when using hostname. Incident overview A subset of Platform customers were unable to launch new PRA sessions when the target machine hostname used a single-label format (e.g, webserver1).

issue: Degradation in incoming traffic. Services behind the NGINX Ingress experienced degraded performance, most notably the Box and Configuration Server services.
root_cause: Date 2026-01-08 Authors Václav Boch, Senior DevOps Engineer Summary We observed a spike in failing requests accompanied by an unusually high volume of error traffic.
solution: The NGINX Ingress is already been marked as deprecated, and several services were migrated to AWS Load Balancers to reduce reliance on the ingress and limit blast radius. This migration prevented further impact on migrated services, while remaining issues were isolated to Box and Configuration Server.

issue: Time to SLA: Degraded performance.
root_cause: Time to SLA is currently experiencing degraded performance caused by elevated API rate limiting from Jira platform.
solution: After an extended observation period, we have confirmed that the implemented changes have successfully mitigated the issue.

issue: Performance Issues. We are moving this incident to Resolved at this time, and will continue to monitor our systems for any further disruptions.

issue: Voice API Intermittent Failures (India Region). The service was not continuously unavailable, but experienced periodic degradation during the incident window.

As a result: The legacy video encoding process did not initiate for uploaded videos Assets did not appear in Asset Manager because they failed validation While affected assets were still available at the origin and accessible via the Rendering and Video APIs, they did not appear in the Asset Manager UI and were not available through the legacy Long-Form Video API.

issue: UCaaS Voice Services Impairment.

issue: Elevated error rates from API.

solution: The errant configuration was identified and corrected and full service was restored in minutes.

issue: GitHub Copilot experienced a service outage with error rates averaging 18% and peaking at 100%.

issue: Increase in release management-related errors.

issue: Issues with accessing Vivantio impacting a small number of customers.

issue: KernelCare NFS Freeze on CL8/EL8.
root_cause: A KernelCare adaptation of the CVE-2025-39697 NFS patch introduced a locking regression. Specifically, the patch caused the same spinlock to be acquired twice within a single execution path: - nfs_page_group_lock - nfs_page_group_sync_on_bit This resulted in a deadlock that left kernel threads stuck in the D state.
solution: Once triggered, the patch could not be safely unloaded, and affected systems either froze indefinitely or rebooted due to hung task watchdogs.

issue: Document Reports not being processed in US. Summary around 10 minutes after restoring service in the EU and CA from the - outage, we go alerted for high error rate in the US region and we noticed the new ML model version was back online in that region.
root_cause: Root Causes A previously rolled back version of an ML model went back live automatically in the US region. The automated canary reversal did not succeed in that region, leaving the deployment in an inconsistent state.
solution: As a result, the model routing labels were not updated as expected during the next forced deployment, and traffic continued to be served by pods running the incorrect model version until we manually rolled back the model in the cluster.

issue: Document report processing disrupted in EU.
root_cause: Summary For the EU region, one critical service struggled to reprocess the traffic affected by a previous faulty release which led to higher Turnaround Time (TaT) for all Document reports created.

Microsoft has reported that while they have restored their affected infrastructure to a healthy state, additional load balancing is required to mitigate persistent impact from the earlier outage that began.

issue: Edu-ID authentication issues. Incident Postmortem: SAML Edu-ID Login Outage Incident Summary | Field | Details | | --- | --- | | Date | – | | Duration | 7 days | | Severity | High — complete SAML Edu-ID login unavailability | | Affected System | Keycloak SAML Edu-ID authentication (Renku realm), Renkulab 2.15.0 | | Status | Resolved.
root_cause: Root Cause Analysis Starting with Keycloak version 21 (introduced in Renkulab 2.14.0, deployed ), Keycloak stopped decrypting SAML assertions that were encrypted using a realm key originally generated for signing purposes.
solution: Keycloak 25 removed the -Dkeycloak.saml.deprecated.encryption=true flag entirely, eliminating the workaround. This resolved the issue for Edu-ID users without a separate academic profile.

issue: Incident with Actions. on August 7, GitHub Actions experienced degraded availability.
root_cause: The incident was triggered by a routine deployment to an internal Actions service responsible for processing events and generating Actions jobs.
solution: As pods were replaced during the deployment, remaining capacity became saturated, causing services to crash and triggering a cascading impact across multiple clusters and downstream services. This second stage of impact was mitigated by deploying changes to prevent runners from repeatedly attempting to acquire invalid jobs.

issue: As the core services recovered, a latent bug in the job-assignment path made recovery slower: runners were handed jobs that had already been revoked, then got stuck retrying them instead of picking up valid work, which created a self-amplifying backlog.
root_cause: A routine deployment that briefly reduced the number of running pods was enough to exhaust available headroom.
solution: Over roughly the next two hours we expanded capacity for the saturated services and throttled incoming webhook-triggered work so the system could stabilize. We deployed fixes so runners stopped trying to acquire invalid jobs, drained the accumulated queues, and raised the internal rate limits that were slowing recovery.

issue: Monitoring - Pipelines Stuck - Prod2. As each pass consumed progressively more memory and CPU without ever completing, the service instance performing that work stopped making progress, and every execution assigned to that instance stalled — which is what customers reported.

solution: Harness engineers identified the cause, mitigated the impact, and pipeline executions returned to normal operation. The majority of pipelines on Prod2 continued to execute successfully throughout the incident; the primary impact was that some in-flight executions could not complete and needed to be re-run once the issue was mitigated.

issue: SEI 2.0 dashboards are not loading. No customer data was lost, and ingestion of all integration data continued to work uninterrupted.

issue: Potential Connected Search Service Disruption. Connected Search and the Lucidworks Platform are fully operational, having experienced no service degradation.

issue: Linux qdisc-rtab-race (CVE-2026-68138): qdisc rate-table UAF to local root. Reliability Exploitation is unreliable and disruptive when it fails — approximately 1 success in 8 attempts, with 6 of the 8 failed attempts causing a kernel oops or hang.

issue: Delayed data processing in the Europe region. Replaying several days of data was the slowest part of the recovery by design, as we rate-limited the replay so that real-time ingestion wasn't put at risk.

solution: Our initial fixes, tuning the write path and adding capacity, restored real-time ingestion within a day, but draining the backlog alongside live traffic re-created the contention. We then rebuilt the recovery pipeline and held live data with strict priority while separately replaying the backlog at a controlled rate.

issue: From 40 seconds to under 10: rebuilding incident detection on OpenTelemetry, Apache Kafka, and Apache Flink on Kubernetes. An error rate or a volume drop that a human would call an incident.
root_cause: Two incidents in one year were caused by another tenant’s lag on the same queue, which is a bad property for the system that is supposed to detect incidents.
solution: This post describes how a small team rebuilt the detection platform behind our automated incident creation (“AutoHOT”, where HOT is our internal name for a high-severity incident) on Apache Kafka, Apache Flink on Kubernetes and OpenTelemetry, what we measured month by month for eighteen months, and what we would do differently. This alone removed a whole class of scaling work and made the topic small enough that seven days of retention is cheap.

issue: Scan Performance Degredation. This occurred during a period of high event volume, which led to the database reaching maximum capacity and slowing down the overall processing workflow.
